statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme
is (quasi-)excellent.

\label{lemma-locally-excellent}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is (quasi-)excellent.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme
is (quasi-)excellent.
